transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how I look, I guess. Since I started helping with safety trainings at work, I notice my hands a lot when I’m pointing—like they look wrinkly or uneven. And then in the newsletter photos, I keep thinking my face looks crooked, even though people say they don’t really see it.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking how your hands or face look?

Yeah… I do some checking. Before I teach a class or go to one of those senior-center workshops, I’ll look in the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face a couple ways. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look okay. It can make me a little late, but I still go.
Do you have thoughts about your appearance that you can't stop thinking about?

Yes… mostly about my hands lately. When I’m pointing during the safety trainings, I keep noticing they look wrinkly or uneven. And then with the newsletter pictures, I get stuck thinking my face looks crooked, even when other people say they don’t really see it.
Do you feel really upset or anxious when you think about how your hands or face look?

Yeah… I do get anxious about it. It’s mostly when I’m pointing during trainings and I notice my hands looking wrinkly or uneven. Then with those newsletter photos, I start thinking my face looks crooked, even if people tell me they don’t see it. It just kind of sticks in my head.
Do these thoughts about your hands and face come into your mind against your will?

Yeah… they do. I don’t really want to think about it, but since I started helping with the safety trainings, I’ll notice my hands when I’m pointing, and it just… sticks. Then I start thinking about my face in those newsletter photos too, like it looks crooked, even though people say they don’t see it.
Do these thoughts about your appearance feel like they are forcing their way into your mind?

Yes… it kind of feels that way. I’ll be doing the training and pointing at something, and then I just can’t stop noticing my hands, like they look wrinkly or uneven. Then I start thinking about the newsletter pictures too, that my face looks crooked… even when people say they don’t see it.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking behaviors to reduce your anxiety about your appearance?

Yeah… I guess I do. Before a class or one of the senior-center workshops, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face different ways… sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look okay. It settles me a little, but then I’m running a bit behind. I still go, though.
Do you think your concerns about your appearance are unreasonable?

I… I know people say they don’t see it, so maybe it is a bit unreasonable. But when I’m pointing during the trainings, my hands just look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And then with the newsletter photos, I keep thinking my face looks crooked. It’s hard to shake it.
Are these thoughts and worries about your appearance affecting your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

A little, yes. It hasn’t really stopped me from work or volunteering… I still do those things. But I’m slower getting ready before trainings, and I’ve started avoiding photos sometimes. I also hesitate more before going to social things I used to just enjoy.
Do you think other people can see these flaws in your appearance that you're worried about?

I’m not sure. People tell me they don’t really see it… but when I’m up there pointing during the safety trainings, my hands look so wrinkly and uneven to me. And in the newsletter pictures, I keep thinking my face looks crooked. So part of me feels like they must notice, even if they say they don’t.
Do you ever have moments where you're able to push these thoughts about your appearance out of your mind?

Sometimes, yes… if I’m busy enough, I can push it aside for a while. But since I started helping with the safety trainings, it keeps coming back—my hands when I’m pointing, and then those newsletter photos where my face looks crooked to me. Even if people say they don’t see it, I still notice it.
Do you believe your appearance flaws are real, even if others can't see them?

I guess… yes, I do. Even when people say they don’t see it, I still notice my hands looking wrinkly and uneven when I’m pointing things out at the trainings. And then in the newsletter photos, my face just looks crooked to me. I know others don’t agree, but it feels real to me.
Do you ever feel like you're trying to ignore these thoughts about your appearance but they just won't leave your mind?

Yes… that’s pretty much why I came in. Since I started helping with the safety trainings, I keep noticing my hands when I’m pointing—how wrinkly and uneven they look. I try not to think about it, but then I see the newsletter photos and start thinking my face looks crooked, even though people say they don’t see it. It just kind of stays with me.
Have you avoided any social or occupational activities because of your concerns about your appearance?

Not really stopped me, no. I still go to work and I still help with the trainings. But… I take longer getting ready for them now, and I’ve started avoiding pictures when I can. Sometimes I hesitate before going to social things I used to just go to without thinking.
Do you feel like your worries about your appearance are interfering with your overall happiness or well-being?

A little, I guess. It hasn’t stopped me from working or helping with the trainings, but I’m slower getting ready now. And I’ve been avoiding photos more… sometimes I pause before going to social things I used to enjoy. So, yes, it does take something away.
Is there one particular part of your body that you're most concerned about?

Mostly my hands, I guess. When I’m pointing things out at the trainings, I notice how wrinkly and uneven they look. And then… sometimes my face too, in those newsletter photos, like it looks crooked, even though people say it doesn’t.
Do you feel like your worries about your appearance are causing you significant distress?

Yes… I mean, not terribly, but it bothers me. It hasn’t stopped me from working or volunteering, but I do take longer getting ready for trainings now, and I try to avoid photos. Sometimes I hesitate before going to social things I used to just go to. So… yes, it does upset me some.
Have your concerns about your appearance ever caused you to avoid important work or social events?

Not really important ones, no. I still go to work and I still help with the trainings. I just… take longer getting ready, and I’ve started avoiding pictures when I can. Sometimes I do hesitate before social things I used to enjoy, but I usually still go.
Do you feel like your concerns about your appearance are driven more by unwanted, intrusive thoughts or by a feeling that you need to perform specific rituals or behaviors to manage your anxiety?

I guess it’s a bit of both, but more like… I feel I have to do certain things or I’ll keep worrying. Before a class or one of the senior-center workshops, I check the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face different ways. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look all right. It can make me run a little behind, but I still go.
Do you feel like your appearance concerns are more about fixing a flaw or more about following a routine to feel right?

More about… trying to fix it, I guess. Or make sure it looks okay. Before a class or the senior-center workshop, I’ll check the bathroom mirror a few times, put lotion on my hands, turn my face a little… sometimes ask a coworker if I look all right. It’s not a big routine exactly, but it can make me run a little behind. I still go, though.
